Single-violation fixture for the exec-output taint scan (TestTaintFindingNamesEscapeOriginRemedy).
One value escapes, into an error in package escape. It was printed by a git
spawn in package spawn, two packages away, through package relay — and it is a
phi of two spawns, so the finding must name both origins, not just the first.
The test finds every line by its anchor comment.

-- spawn.go --
package spawn

import "os/exec"

// Head is what git printed, from one of two invocations.
func Head(short bool) string {
	var out []byte
	if short {
		out, _ = exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD").Output() // anchor: spawn-short
	} else {
		out, _ = exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD").Output() // anchor: spawn-long
	}
	return string(out)
}

-- relay.go --
package relay

import "example.com/fixture/spawn"

// Describe wraps the head in prose; the relay is where a per-package scan
// would lose the thread.
func Describe(short bool) string {
	return "head is " + spawn.Head(short)
}

-- escape.go --
package escape

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"example.com/fixture/relay"
)

// Check quotes the head into an error: the one violation.
func Check(short bool) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("unexpected %s", relay.Describe(short)) // anchor: escape
}

// Run is Check's caller, so the error's return is not itself an edge.
func Run() {
	if err := Check(len(os.Args) > 1); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
	}
}
